LESSON: GYMNASTICS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.6: Gymnastics
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Gymnastics, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: Why are sequences performed in Gymnastics?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Gymnastics together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: learner acquires the skills of cartwheel, roll and balance to be able to perform a 3-action sequence in

gymnastics.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner practises and creates different 3-action sequences of a gymnastics

performance.

• Self - efficacy: the learner's self-esteem is enhanced by being able to perform a 3-action sequence in gymnastics.

Values:
• Responsibility: as learners put into practise the aspects of safety, while performing 3-action sequence in gymnastics.

• Love: The learner respects others as they practise the combination of gymnastics progressions to form a 3- action sequence

in gymnastics.

21

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Gender: The learner works with peers in groups (boys and girls) while they create and improvise the floor mats and perform

the 3- action sequence in gymnastics.

• Safety: The learner observes safety as they perform cartwheel, rolls, balances and to form a 3- action sequence of a gymnastic

performance.

Link to other learning areas:

Science and Technology: The learner applies the concept of how the body works during performance of gymnastic activity.

Suggested learning resources

Floor mats, whistle, spotting blocks, props and balances, balance beams, pods, bars and rings, grips, straps, fitness balls, cones,

markers, yarns, polythene materials, fibres, wood/timber, nails, hammer, needles, threads, video clips on cartwheel
